reason: The cited evidence does not address the effect of Ti on SFE in CoCrFeNiTi, nor does it provide data on dislocation mobility, cross-slip, or dynamic recovery in this alloy. E1 discusses general deformation challenges in CrMnFeCoNi, and E2 describes deformation mechanisms in a dual-phase HEA, neither supporting the key premises.
premises: Ti addition to CoCrFeNi increases stacking fault energy (SFE)
Higher SFE promotes cross-slip and dislocation mobility
Single-phase solid-solution state enables rapid dynamic recovery
Rapid dynamic recovery and high mobility prevent dislocation accumulation and forest hardening
These mechanisms explain low hardness/strength in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi
